hints: Focus on what sp2 really means, a carbon with one double bond and three sigma regions in a flat arrangement.
Write the structure with double bonds shown as CH2=CH-CH2-CH=C=CH-CH3 and label C1 to C7 from left to right.
Look closely at the C=C=C middle section, one of those three carbons is different from a normal alkene carbon and is not sp2.
walkthrough:
**Draw the double bonds in place**

Think of the name first. Hept-1,4,5-triene means a 7-carbon chain with double bonds starting at C1, C4 and C5.

Displayed skeleton:
$$\text{CH}_2=\text{CH}-\text{CH}_2-\text{CH}=\text{C}=\text{CH}-\text{CH}_3$$
$$C1\quad C2\quad C3\quad C4\quad C5\quad C6\quad C7$$

**Recall the hybridisation rule**

A friendly rule that always works: count sigma regions around carbon.

$$\text{sp}^3: 4 \text{ single bonds, tetrahedral} \quad \text{sp}^2: 1 \text{ double bond + 2 singles, trigonal planar} \quad \text{sp}: 2 \text{ double bonds or 1 triple bond, linear}$$

**Sort each carbon**

C1 ($\text{CH}_2=$) has one double bond, so sp2. C2 ($\text{=CH}-$) has one double bond, so sp2.

C3 ($\text{-CH}_2-$) has only single bonds, so sp3. C4 ($\text{-CH}= $) has one double bond, so sp2.

**Handle the allene centre carefully**

C5 ($\text{=C=} $) has two double bonds, one to each side. That makes it linear sp, not sp2. This is the classic trap.

C6 ($\text{=CH}-$) has one double bond, so sp2. C7 ($\text{-CH}_3$) has only singles, so sp3.

**Count the sp2 carbons**

Sp2 carbons are C1, C2, C4 and C6 only.

$$1 + 1 + 0 + 1 + 0 + 1 + 0 = 4 \text{ sp}^2 \text{ carbons}$$

options.A: Correct. C1, C2, C4 and C6 each have one C=C double bond and are trigonal planar sp2. C3 and C7 are sp3, and the central allene carbon C5 is sp. Total is 4.
options.B: Incorrect. This counts 5 by wrongly including the central allene carbon C5 as sp2. C5 forms two double bonds ($\text{C}=\text{C}=\text{C}$) so it is linear sp hybridised, not sp2.
options.C: Incorrect. This counts all the carbons involved in multiple bonds (C1, C2, C4, C5, C6) plus one extra, forgetting that single-bond CH2 and CH3 carbons (C3 and C7) are sp3 and that C5 is sp.
options.D: Incorrect. This assumes every carbon in a triene must be sp2 because the name contains 'ene'. It ignores that saturated CH2 and CH3 carbons are sp3 and that a cumulated C=C=C system contains an sp carbon.
